Generate A Tapestry-Style Pooling Matrix

Source: R/tapestry_hyperec.R
tapestry_matrix.Rd

Construct a Tapestry-style pooling design in which each individual is placed in exactly three pools and the resulting matrix is intended for quantitative compressed-sensing reconstruction rather than binary COMP decoding.

Usage

tapestry_matrix(
  n,
  k = NULL,
  method = c("random", "kirkman"),
  prevalence = 0.01
)

Arguments

n

Integer scalar giving the total number of individuals. This is the column dimension \(N\) of the returned pooling matrix and must satisfy \(N \ge 1\).

k

Optional integer scalar giving the expected number of positive individuals used to size the number of pools. If NULL, the function uses \(k = \max\{1, \lfloor N \cdot \texttt{prevalence}\rfloor\}\).

method

Character string specifying the construction rule: "kirkman" for a Kirkman-triple-inspired layout or "random" for a random triple assignment. The default is "random".

prevalence

Numeric scalar giving the expected prevalence used only when k is NULL. The default is 0.01.

Value

A named list with components:

matrix

A sparse binary matrix of class dgCMatrix with dimensions \(J \times N\)

m

The realized number of pools \(J\)

n

The number of individuals \(N\)

lambda_max

The target maximum column sum, fixed at 3

method

The construction rule actually used

design_type

"tapestry"

The matrix itself also carries a design attribute with fields type, n, m, lambda_max, k_expected, and method.

Details

Tapestry is a single-round design aimed at quantitative pooled measurements and compressed-sensing-style reconstruction rather than binary COMP decoding. In the package-wide notation, observed pool outcomes are denoted by \(\mathbf{z}\). This help page adopts a decoder-local compressed-sensing notation, standard for the Tapestry literature, in which \(\mathbf{A}\) is the design matrix, \(\mathbf{x}\) is the unknown sparse signal, \(\mathbf{y}\) is the response vector, and \(\mathbf{g}\) is the measurement-noise vector. In that local notation, $$\mathbf{y} = \mathbf{A}\mathbf{x} + \mathbf{g}.$$

This constructor places each individual in exactly three pools, so the intended maximum column sum is \(\lambda_{\max} = 3\). The current package implementation provides either a Kirkman-triple-inspired layout or a random triple assignment. It returns only the constructed matrix object and associated metadata; it does not implement a quantitative decoder.

Construction Methods

method = "kirkman"

Uses the package's Kirkman-triple-inspired assignment path.

method = "random"

Uses a random triple assignment while keeping each individual in exactly three pools.

References

Ghosh, S., Agarwal, R., Rehan, M. A., et al. (2021). Tapestry: A single-round smart pooling technique for COVID-19 testing. Nature Communications, 12, Article 2995.

Ghosh, S., et al. (2021). A compressed sensing approach to pooled RT-PCR testing for COVID-19 detection. IEEE Open Journal of Signal Processing, 2, 248-264. doi:10.1109/OJSP.2021.3075913
